newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Institutional investors keen on Israel's Comfy.
newsitem.headline: Institutional investors keen on Israel's Comfy.

text.p: The precommitment tranche of a public offering by Israeli toymaker Comfy Interactive Movies Ltd was heavily oversubscribed as foreign institutions put in for $31.5 million worth of shares, the underwriter said on Monday.

Roger Hornett of Societe Generale Strauss Turnbull Securities, which is the international distributor of the Tel Aviv offering as well as one of three underwriters, said Comfy is seeking to raise $29.3 million.
The tender will open on Thursday with the filing of a prospectus and close on June 5.

"We were asked to secure precommitments to the sum of half of the value of $29.3 million in the U.K. and continental Europe. We closed precommitments on Friday with $31.5 million of interest from 37 major institutions and with additional interest in the tender," Hornett told Reuters.
"Foreign institutions effectively have underwritten the issue," Hornett said.
The three-year-old company makes the Comfy keyboard, a computer peripheral for toddlers aged one to three, as well as interactive software for young children.
It is a rare instance of a high-tech start-up opting to float domestically rather than on Nasdaq.
"We believe Nasdaq is vulnerable. We think there will be a correction at some point. Tel Aviv is looking extremely sound," Hornett said.
"There is no overheating in the new issues market...Israel is the home of high-tech and it's time to bring the culture home," Hornett said.

The company will issue 12.5 million new shares priced at eight shekels each. There are currently 31.18 million shares outstanding held by Shamrock Holdings, the investment arm of the Roy Disney family, as well as Bank Hapoalim, Israeli investment bank Dovrat Shrem and Cowen & Co.
Comfy will have a market capitalisation after the offering of $102.6 million.
Hornett said this was the first fixed-price tender in Tel Aviv as well as the first issue with a foreign broker leading the underwriting.

Comfy's sales last year doubled to $3.8 million with a gross profit of $1.5 million but a net loss of $2.2 million. "The company beefed up financial management and on first-quarter figures, if sales were to be unchanged, it would roughly break even," Hornett said.
Comfy has signed a deal with MGM-United Artists for an interactive movie called "House of Numbers", featuring the Pink Panther and aimed at helping children learn to count.
Comfy has also signed terms of agreement with JVC (Victor Co of Japan) to launch a new family computer, which plugs into a television set, at a multimedia trade fair in Atlanta in June.
"JVC forecasts sales of one million units a year and each one will have a piece of Comfy software," Hornett said.
